subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Dribbling, Passing, and Foot Skills in Small-Sided Play
title: Reteach and varied practice: passing to space rather than to a person
focus: passing to space rather than to a person
essentialQuestion: How do I keep and move an object as a team?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Pass ahead of a moving teammate into the space they are running into.
Judge their speed before you release.
Call it so they know it is coming.
A pass to space only works if someone is moving there.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Passing to a stationary teammate feet every time. Fix: award the cooperative goal only for passes received on the move.
keyPoints: Pass ahead of a moving teammate into the space they are running into.
Judge their speed before you release.
Call it so they know it is coming.
A pass to space only works if someone is moving there.
privacySafeScenario: Play a small-sided cooperative game and explain two decisions you made about space and support.
studentTask: The learner practises passing to space rather than to a person at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with passing to space rather than to a person and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about passing to space rather than to a person at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for passing to space rather than to a person.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Foot-skill tasks may be done with a stationary ball, a slower rolled ball, a larger ball, a hand or assistive device in place of the foot, or from a seated position. Travel distance is always adjustable.
extensionChallenge: Apply passing to space rather than to a person under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises passing to space rather than to a person. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
